// as empty, contents-hidden stubs, regardless of ignore files. Viewers can see
// the folder exists, but nothing inside it is watched, hashed, or uploaded.
// defaultPatterns apply to every broadcast, beneath any ignore file. Share
// links are public, so common credential files are excluded; a .gitignore or
// patternFiles are read from every directory, in order, so .bigaignore rules
// override .gitignore rules in the same directory.
// IsStubDir reports whether a directory with the given base name is shown as
// IsPatternFile reports whether a file with the given base name holds ignore
// patterns, so a change to it changes what the filter accepts.
// Package config resolves runtime settings from the environment.
// DefaultAPIURL is the server used when BIGA_API_URL is unset. Release builds
// Timing holds the knobs that dominate the latency between a save and a
// viewer seeing it. Defaults are tuned for a near-live feel; each can be raised
// for slow disks or filesystems that report noisy partial writes.
// Idle is the quiet gap after the last change before a checkpoint is sent.
// MaxWait caps how long a sustained burst of edits can delay a checkpoint.
// Stability is how long a file must stop changing before it is read, which
// guards against uploading a half-written file.
// Config is the resolved runtime configuration.
// APIURL is the server base URL without a trailing slash.
// Home is the directory holding local state, normally ~/.biga.
// Heartbeat is how often a broadcast tells the server it is still live. It
// must stay well under the server's staleness window.
// UpdateCheck reports whether to look for newer releases.
// Load reads the configuration using getenv, normally [os.Getenv].
// NormalizeAPIURL validates an http(s) base URL and strips trailing slashes.
must be an http or https URL"
// millis parses a positive integer count of milliseconds, falling back when
// the value is unset or invalid.
// Batcher coalesces changed paths into batches. A batch is flushed once
// changes stop for the idle duration, or after maxWait during a sustained
// burst. Flushes run one at a time, in the order their batches closed, so
// checkpoint uploads never overlap or reorder.
// A Batcher starts paused: paths added before [Batcher.Start] accumulate and
// flushing is a one-slot semaphore held for the whole of each flush, from
// taking the batch to the callback returning. A channel rather than a
// mutex, because waiters can be parked behind a slow upload.
// NewBatcher returns a paused batcher that hands each batch to flush. The
// callback may call [Batcher.Add] to requeue paths that failed to sync.
// Add marks paths as changed. It is a no-op after [Batcher.Close].
// Start begins flushing; ctx is passed to every flush.
// Close flushes whatever is pending, waits for any flush in progress, and
// stops the batcher. Paths requeued by that final flush are dropped.
// Command biga broadcasts a local directory so others can watch it live.
Broadcast a local directory so others can watch it change in real time. There
are no accounts or sign-in: the session ID is the share link.
